_comment: Inventory of every modification this fork carries inside upstream-owned files. See AGENTS.md. Seeded 2026-08-26 from fork/main c0123f6d. The count is the number to drive down. platform#z5x2's main.go component has landed: every main.go site is now a bodyless hook and the file's deletions fell 35 -> 6 (the irreducible set: 3 module-rename import paths, the install-once closure body, and the two http.ListenAndServe* calls that name upstream's s). Inventory entries for main.go rose 12 -> 13 (16 marker lines over 13 slugs; the entry count is what this file tracks, never the raw marker count -- AGENTS.md rule 4). The extra entry is deliberate -- exec-denial-wiring was split into exec-denial-authorizer and exec-denial-schema-resolver, because merging two security gates into one call site is how a fail-open gets built (AGENTS.md rule 4). Components 2 (pkg/query) and 3 (pkg/server) are still outstanding, in that order.

entries.why: platformauth import; the two exec-denial option hooks and the middleware wrap all name it
hardened-mode flags must be declared on the default FlagSet before upstream's flag.Parse
fail-fast flag-combination checks must run after flag.Parse and before any resource is allocated
install-once state is created once, not per connection; only the closure body changes, upstream's NewConnector call and brace are byte-identical

the data plane's query options are unconditional, so they append after upstream's assembly rather than replacing it. SYNC HAZARD: this line names upstream's queryOptions local. A rename upstream merges with NO conflict (the hunks are disjoint) and leaves this line dangling -- deleting it as dead code silently drops the reviewed function allowlist and remote-URI-literal rejection. Re-point it at the new name; never delete it. Always run go build -tags=duckdb_arrow after a trial merge -- but note go build does NOT catch the deletion, only the rename: platform_test.go's TestMainGoRetainsLoadBearingHookCode is what turns the deletion red

latch must fire after INSTALL and before any query-serving connection; ordering is the security property. SYNC HAZARD: this hook is textually disjoint from the upstream code it sits between, so a merge resolution can drop it with NO conflict and a green go build, after which DuckDB external access stays on for the whole process in default mode. Never delete it; platform_test.go's TestMainGoRetainsLoadBearingHookCode is the only check that catches the loss
bootstrap must start before the public listener and its connection is held for the process lifetime via defer in run()
validator construction; audience is hardcoded in platform.go, never operator-settable

gate 1 of three independent exec denials; deliberately kept separate from the resolver hook (AGENTS.md rule 4 -- merging them produced a fail-open in a dry run). SYNC HAZARD: this hook is one argument inside upstream's server.New call, so a merge resolution can drop it with NO conflict and a green go build, after which gate 1 is gone and nothing else fails. Never delete it; platform_test.go's TestMainGoRetainsLoadBearingHookCode is the only check that catches the loss

gate 2 of three; arms the schema-policy guard in pkg/server's execCommand. SYNC HAZARD: this hook is one argument inside upstream's server.New call, so a merge resolution can drop it with NO conflict and a green go build -- and the loss is worse than gate 2 alone, because pkg/server/server.go's CommandExec guard then sees a nil resolver, goes false, and re-enables exec. Never delete it; platform_test.go's TestMainGoRetainsLoadBearingHookCode is the only check that catches the loss
wraps the server handler in JWT middleware; every request must carry a validated session before it reaches s
hardened-mode fields are added beside upstream's literal so its 14 rows stay byte-identical; the log must never carry the Quack fd, token or session header
listener serves the wrapped handler; upstream names s directly so this cannot be additive
